label: <DEL> step when the sequence begins with p/q/g/2 (also i/3)
explanation: Fires almost only at the delimiter step (88% of activation mass; 10.5% of <DEL> steps are active). Which <DEL> steps fire depends on the first original tokens, i.e. the token about to be recalled first: first_tok/out_tok in {p,q,g,2} gives 4-8x lift, {i,3,s,t} weaker. Precision is 0.96 when both orig(0) and orig(1) are in {p,q,g,2}, so the dependence looks graded and position-weighted rather than a clean set. Longer sequences (L=8,9) fire more often and more strongly. A smaller part of the mass (~10%) is on original-phase input e (first occurrence). It does not fire in the copy phase or at t=0. The predicate gets F1 ~0.45 because many <DEL> steps whose sequence starts with other tokens still fire weakly, and many p/q/g/2-initial <DEL> steps do not fire.
